title: HealFlow: automated remediation playbook and upgrade glidepath for Private VPCs
creator: Ava Patel
description: Create a comprehensive runbook and automated remediation workflow (HealFlow) for common Private (VPC) healthcheck failures. This ticket covers Terraform preflight/sentinel-style guards, in-cluster validators, automated heal actions (repair terraform state, restart/replace agents, reroute traffic), and a safe upgrade glidepath that prevents mass disruption during Private node upgrades.
reproduction_steps: 1) Deploy a Private VPC using terraform modules from infra/private/v1 with default autoscaling=on.
2) Simulate a degraded node: remove a node from the ASG or introduce circuit-breaker errors by blocking egress to the model cache endpoint.
3) Trigger the platform vpc-healthcheck endpoint to surface failing metrics (healthcheck returns non-200 for probe 'agent-heartbeat' and 'kv-cache-presence').
4) Observe Terraform drift if operator manually modifies cloud routes without terraform apply.
automated_playbook_steps: Step A - Preflight checks (Terraform plan guard): run 'terraform plan -out=plan.tfplan' and a custom preflight script (scripts/preflight_check.sh) that validates IAM, subnets, route tables and KMS policies. If preflight fails, abort and create an advisory in #private-ops.

Step B - Validation probe: run the cluster validator job (kubectl -n redwood run validator --image=redwood/validator:stable) to collect agent metrics, KV cache status, network egress tests, and node kubelet readiness. Store probe report to S3: s3://redwood-private/healthchecks/<run-id>.json.
- If agent-heartbeat missing for a single node AND autoscaler reports replaced instance, mark as 'self-healed' and close runbook automatically.
- If KV cache warm fail or prefix mismatch, attempt 'kv-cache-warm --target <node>' up to 2 retries, then trigger cache rebuild job that streams prefix snapshots from primary region.
- If network egress blocked, provision temporary NAT gateway via terraform patch module 'vpc/nat-temporary' with short TTL and notify security for follow-up.

Step D - Terraform reconciliation: run a targeted terraform apply with 'terraform apply -target=module.agent_pool -auto-approve' when resources are out-of-sync, and record plan output in the incident ticket. Use a sentinel-style check to block >30% simultaneous replacements.

Step E - Upgrade glidepath: execute canary upgrade of agent image on a single AZ, run full suite of health probes for 15 minutes, then gradually increase to 25%/50%/100% with cooldown windows and the ability to abort via flag 'healflow.abort=true'.
observability_checks: Critical charts to inspect: agent_heartbeat_missing, kv_cache_hit_rate, vpc_dropped_packets, terraform_drift_alert_count
Tracer hooks: attach probe-id to request traces (trace.probe_id) and correlate with console-2026.03 rollout dashboard
Log searches: 'agent restart', 'kubelet crashloop', 'failed to warm kv cache' over the last 30m
Synthetic probes: run curl https://internal-vpc-probe.redwood/api/health with header X-Probe-ID to validate route tables from multiple subnets
rollback_strategy: 1) Abort upgrade/canary and roll agents back to previous image using deployment revision: 'kubectl rollout undo deployment/agent -n redwood --to-revision=<stable-rev>'.

2) Restore terraform-managed resources from the last applied state: 'terraform state pull' and if drift detected run 'terraform apply' against the saved plan. Only patch sensitive resources after security review.
3) If KV cache rebuild fails, route traffic to warm-region via smart routing policy and create a high-priority job to rehydrate cache from snapshot.
4) For repeated node flapping, cordon node, drain pods, and mark as quarantined in inventory; create follow-up engineering task to replace AMI or instance type.
5) Ensure all remediation actions emit an audit event to audit-log S3 and to the private-console timeline for customer-facing incident notes.
acceptance_criteria: Runbook covers at least 6 common failure modes with clear play/action mapping (agent heartbeat, kv-cache, egress, terraform drift, AMI/instance failures, load-balancer health).
HealFlow orchestrator can perform preflight, validation probe, and at least 4 automated remediation actions without human intervention under test harness.
Upgrade glidepath includes canary, staged rollout, abort flag, and automated rollback for failed probes.
Preflight terraform guard blocks destructive plans that would replace >30% of capacity without manual override and emits human-readable rationale.
Documentation (Confluence runbook) and 1-page run-through are published and reviewed by SRE and Security with sign-off.
